about.title: Manhattan Beach Slip & Fall Claims
about.longDescription: Manhattan Beach draws heavy foot traffic to its beachfront businesses, sandy walkways, and pier-area shops, all of which create the kind of surfaces where a slip, trip, or fall can happen fast. Whether the fall occurred on wet tile near a restaurant patio, a cracked sidewalk off Manhattan Beach Boulevard, or a poorly lit stairwell in a retail building, California law asks a specific question: did the property owner know, or should they have known, about the hazard, and did they fail to fix or warn about it? That's the heart of a premises liability claim here. Because evidence like surveillance footage, incident reports, and maintenance logs can disappear quickly, acting early matters. LawProactive doesn't practice law itself; we simply connect you with an independent, local attorney who can evaluate what happened, gather the right proof, and explain your options, all without any upfront cost to you.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney About a Fall Claim

items.title: Notice Has to Be Proven
items.desc: California requires showing the property owner knew or reasonably should have known about the hazard before your fall. An attorney knows how to dig up maintenance records, prior complaints, or repair history to build that proof.

items.title: Video and Records Disappear Fast
items.desc: Surveillance footage at stores and business properties is often overwritten within days or weeks. Getting a preservation request out quickly can be the difference between having evidence and having none.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Cut Both Ways
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly at fault, though your share of fault reduces what you receive. An attorney can help make sure your side of the story is documented fairly from the start.

items.question: How long do I have to file a slip and fall claim in Manhattan Beach?
items.answer: Generally, California gives you two years from the date of the fall to file a personal injury lawsuit. If the property involved is owned by a public entity, such as a city sidewalk or municipal building, the deadline is much shorter and requires an early claim. It's worth having an attorney confirm which timeline applies to your situation as soon as possible.

items.question: I fell at a business near the pier and no one filled out a report. Does that hurt my claim?
items.answer: It's not ideal, but it's not fatal to your case either. Photos of the hazard, witness names, and even a follow-up call or email to the business describing what happened can help fill that gap. An attorney can help gather what's still available and explain what other evidence might strengthen your claim.

items.question: What if the store says the spill I slipped on was cleaned up quickly?
items.answer: That's a common response, but it doesn't automatically end your claim. The question is whether the business had a reasonable system for spotting and cleaning hazards, and whether that system failed here. An independent attorney can request cleaning logs, employee schedules, and any video to see whether that explanation holds up.
